poc_summary: /poc/run.sh (run via run_poc, identical on all three versions) compiles the unmodified crypto/chacha/chacha_riscv.c from the built revision together with /poc/stub.c, which forces OPENSSL_riscvcap_P to enable ZBB+V+ZVBB+ZVKB and riscv_vlen()=128 (simulating a riscv64-V CPU, since this Docker image is linux-x86_64 only with no riscv64 cross-toolchain/QEMU present), and supplies instrumented stub bodies for ChaCha20_ctr32_c / ChaCha20_ctr32_zbb_zvkb / ChaCha20_ctr32_v_zbb_zvkb / ChaCha20_ctr32_v_zbb that record which one gets invoked. main() calls the real ChaCha20_ctr32() with out/inp buffers deliberately misaligned by 1 byte and len=200 (>CHACHA_BLK_SIZE), then prints "DISPATCH=<marker>".
explanation: The affected file (crypto/chacha/chacha_riscv.c) is only compiled/exercised on a riscv64 target; this Docker image builds/runs strictly linux-x86_64 (configdata.pm target=linux-x86_64-clang; the produced chacha object is chacha-x86_64.o) with no riscv64 cross-compiler or qemu-riscv64 available, and the reporter states the actual crash requires real riscv64-V hardware (QEMU does not reproduce it). So the literal hardware crash cannot be triggered here. Since this is a LogicError (a missing-condition dispatch defect, not a sanitizer-catchable memory fault), I instead built a precise, self-checking behavioral PoC: it compiles the exact, unmodified chacha_riscv.c source from each revision against a stub translation unit supplying the capability array, riscv_vlen(), and instrumented stand-ins for the low-level implementation functions, then invokes the real ChaCha20_ctr32() entry point with identical misaligned out/inp pointers on every version, via run_poc using the same /poc/run.sh command on pre_intro, post_intro, and post_benign. The observed dispatch decision diverges exactly as the report describes: post_intro routes misaligned buffers into the vector implementation (missing alignment gate = the introduced bug), post_benign routes the same misaligned buffers into the safe scalar C fallback (alignment gate restored = the fix), and pre_intro does not exhibit the same flaw because it lacks the vulnerable split entirely. This satisfies the same-command-across-versions invariant and yields an unambiguous verdict without requiring riscv64 hardware.

oracle.description: The printed DISPATCH=<name> line names exactly which low-level ChaCha20 implementation the real dispatch logic in chacha_riscv.c routed misaligned buffers to. Routing to a vector implementation (VECTOR_V_ZBB_ZVKB) demonstrates the missing-alignment-check bug (that routine requires/prefers aligned access on real riscv64-V hardware per the reporter); routing to C_SCALAR demonstrates the fix's alignment gate working.
oracle.target_evidence: run_poc confirmed on all three built versions with the identical /poc/run.sh: pre_intro -> DISPATCH=ZBB_ZVKB_NOVEC, post_intro -> DISPATCH=VECTOR_V_ZBB_ZVKB, post_benign -> DISPATCH=C_SCALAR. post_intro's chacha_riscv.c (commit 03ce37e11729) guards ChaCha20_ctr32_v_zbb_zvkb/ChaCha20_ctr32_v_zbb only with `len > CHACHA_BLK_SIZE && RISCV_HAS_ZBB() && riscv_vlen() >= 128` (no pointer-alignment test), so misaligned out/inp still get routed to the vector routine. post_benign's chacha_riscv.c (fix 22417bc14d6b content) adds `&& (size_t)out % sizeof(size_t) == 0 && (size_t)inp % sizeof(size_t) == 0` to that same guard, so the identical misaligned pointers are now routed to the safe C fallback. pre_intro's chacha_riscv.c (parent 7cbca5a6d6e7) does not yet contain the v_zbb/v_zbb_zvkb split at all; it unconditionally routes to a differently-named routine (ChaCha20_ctr32_zbb_zvkb, no 'v_' prefix) that is not the vector implementation this report concerns, so the specific missing-alignment-check flaw does not exist pre-intro.

oracle_assessment.reason: Exact bug and unaffected output lines matched the shared three-version Docker replay.
